question: What NCR waterways were named in DENR-NCR's 2025 Gawad Taga-Ilog field validation, and how should the earlier 18-item discovery checkpoint be interpreted without conflating waterbodies, stations, watersheds, parks, and habitat contexts?
method: Reviewed the official DENR-NCR indexed text for the 2025 Gawad Taga-Ilog field-validation article and current water-resource preparedness article; direct requests to both pages returned HTTP 403, and no access control was bypassed or local copy retained. Crosswalked the article's printed city/municipality names to the PSA-rendered 2025 NCR city and municipality directories, whose 17-unit name/code comparison is recorded in the linked denominator review. Compared names only against the 2024 Pasig assessment refresh and the 2026-10-24 discovery checkpoint. This records selected source-named waterways and administrative locality context; it does not create canonical features, waterbody boundaries, species observations, or complete regional coverage.

gawadTagaIlog2025.reportedPeriod: Field validation throughout April and early May 2025
gawadTagaIlog2025.scope: Twelve nominated waterways across Metro Manila were assessed for a DENR-NCR recognition program. The page associates each nomination with a reported city or municipality and selected barangays.
gawadTagaIlog2025.accessLimit: Official search-index text exposed the article and all twelve entries; direct page retrieval returned HTTP 403. Full page HTML, maps, photographs, methods for fish assessment, and any geometry were not retrieved.
gawadTagaIlog2025.interpretation: These are selected waterway nominations and program-validation sites, not a complete NCR hydrologic inventory, a fish survey, or an all-waterbody denominator.

waterResourceSystems.accessLimit: Official search-index text reviewed; direct page retrieval returned HTTP 403. The article's visible indexed text does not provide a station register or feature geometry.
waterResourceSystems.interpretation: The three names are system-level monitoring groupings. The stated 89 river-system stations and separate 377 EMB-NCR ambient water-quality stations are monitoring locations, not counts of distinct rivers, waterbodies, or fishing sites.

previousPasigAssessment.interpretation: The five point names are sampling stations on the Pasig main-river assessment, not five additional waterbodies. The assessment names a selected river-system scope and does not give a complete NCR denominator or a species-by-waterway table in the reviewed text.

reconstructedGroups.description: Pasig River, three named major tributaries, and seven named Manila esteros from the 2024 DENR assessment scope.
La Mesa Watershed, Las Piñas-Parañaque Wetland Park, Baseco Lagoon, and Tanza Marine Tree Park from the DENR-NCR environment campaign lead.
Shared-water contexts Manila Bay and Laguna de Bay.
La Mesa Reservoir, a water-storage feature named separately from La Mesa Watershed.

priorCheckpointDisposition.countDisposition: The historical count of 18 is a reconstructed mixed set of waterway names, shared waters, a reservoir, a watershed, a protected wetland park, and a marine-tree-park habitat. It must not be described as 18 validated waterbodies or a complete inventory. The five DENR sampling-point labels are subsites and were not counted as additional waterbodies. The later BMB Jamboree Lake and Ninoy Aquino Parks and Wildlife Center pond rows are two further source-row candidates held separately; the park name does not identify an individual pond.

nominatedWaterways.reportedLocality: Barangay 168 (Dolmar II) to Barangay 167 (Dolmar I), Caloocan City
Barangays Buting and San Joaquin, Pasig City
nominatedWaterways.nameCrosswalk: Exact source-name overlap with the 2024 DENR Pasig assessment; this adds a program locality context, not a new river feature.
Possible name overlap with the 2024 assessment's shorter label 'Paco'; retain as a held name-variant crosswalk rather than merging by text alone.

nominatedWaterways.sourceSpellingNote: Preserve the indexed article's apparent 'Rbgy.' typo in source quotation; the city-level match does not resolve the barangay wording.

limitations: The 2025 Gawad Taga-Ilog list is a selected program nomination set and cannot stand in for a complete NCR waterbody inventory or proof that omitted waterways do not exist.

PSA codes crosswalk the printed city/municipality only. Barangay strings are preserved as source context and were not independently crosswalked; city codes do not locate a waterway or define its route or boundary.
The source page text was available through official search indexing, but direct page retrieval returned HTTP 403; no full HTML or local source snapshot is available.
The DENR monitoring articles describe grouped systems and monitoring sites, not unique feature counts. Their station totals must not be added to waterbody counts.

The prior checkpoint's 18 items mix waterway, shared-water, reservoir, watershed, protected wetland, and habitat contexts; it is not a verified count. The 12 new program nominations also do not complete the inventory.
Estero de Paco and the earlier report label Paco are retained as a possible alias only. No feature merge or identity claim is made.
No fish species, fish presence or absence, fishing access, legal permission, safety, salinity, current water quality, abundance, or public-app claim is supported by this crosswalk.
The NCR source sweep remains incomplete across the 17 administrative units and freshwater, brackish, and marine habitats.
nextAction: Continue source discovery for omitted waterway and wetland classes across all 17 NCR units, then reconcile source names and locality context through independent records before creating canonical feature links. Retrieve a lawful station register or suitable geodata with reuse terms before any route geometry; keep the 2025 selected nominations separate from fish evidence and public mapping.
